brief.title: Advances in IC Engines
brief.audience: M.Tech. Automotive Engineering students, Work Integrated Learning Programmes Division (working professionals in the automotive industry)
textbooks: T1: Internal combustion engine fundamentals by J.B. Heywood
T2: Engineering Fundamentals of the Internal combustion engines by Willard W. Pulkrabek
R1: Gasoline Engine Management by Konrad Reif Ed
R2: Diesel Engine Management (Systems & Components) by Konrad Reif
R3: Internal combustion Engines – Coiln R.Ferguson
brief.notes: Performance and emissions Engine design and operating parameters, Thermodynamic cycles, Gas exchange processes in internal combustion engines, Fluid Motion within combustion chamber, Turbocharging, Fuel injection systems and charge motion for gasoline engines, Fuel injection systems for diesel engines, Combustion in gasoline engines, Combustion in diesel engines, Engine Management systems, Exhaust Gas After treatment, On-board diagnostics, Engine cooling and lubrication Handout course no: AE ZG516; credit units 4; version 3.0 (15-January-2025); instructor Sajeeth Kumar M M. T-ids are textbooks, R-ids reference books. Handout Part B sessions: 1 Emissions; 2 Exhaust gas after treatment; 3 Engine Design and Operating parameters; 4 Air intake Exhaust; 5 SI Engine Fuel metering and Mixture formation; 6 Charger motion within the cylinder; 7 Combustion in SI Engines; 8 Combustion in CI Engines; 9 Engine cycles; 10 Engine Operating characteristics; 11 Alternate fuels; 12 Engine heat transfer and Friction /Lubrication; 13 Legislations, OBD; 14 Engine Calibration; 15 Engine Diagnostics; 16 Buffer Session. Handout experiential component: Virtual Lab with the AMESIM software tool, 12 hours of lab lecture and 20 hours of practice. contactHours = the 15 planned 90-minute sessions; the handout's credit-model line is blank.

topics: Build Your Engine - Architecture, Power, Thermodynamics
Build Your Engine - Breathing & Control Systems
modules.note: Gamified introduction to engine architecture, power fundamentals, breathing, and control systems Module outcome mo-1-1: Analyze engine architecture choices, calculate fundamental performance parameters (displacement, BMEP, thermal efficiency), and differentiate between torque and power to select appropriate engine configurations for specific applications Module outcome mo-1-2: Explain the 4-stroke cycle, calculate and evaluate volumetric efficiency, describe engine control system architecture, and diagnose basic control system failures

modules.title: Performance & Calibration Excellence
modules.note: Performance analysis, calibration strategies, and optimization for SI and CI engines Module outcome mo-2-1: Calculate thermal efficiency, BSFC, and specific outputs from performance data, interpret torque and power curves, and analyze the effects of operating parameters Module outcome mo-2-2: Apply spark timing, fuel metering, VVT, injection timing, EGR, and boost control strategies to calibrate SI and CI engines

modules.title: Air & Fuel Systems - The Foundation of Good Combustion
modules.note: Air intake, boosting, fuel injection, mixture formation, and charge motion Module outcome mo-3-1: Analyze factors affecting volumetric efficiency, design and evaluate turbocharging systems including matching and boost control Module outcome mo-3-2: Compare fuel injection technologies, calculate mixture ratios, and analyze multiple injection strategies for combustion optimization Module outcome mo-3-3: Differentiate between swirl, tumble, and squish, design charge motion strategies, and analyze interaction with fuel injection

modules.title: Combustion Processes - Where the Magic Happens
modules.note: SI combustion, CI combustion, advanced cycles and combustion modes Module outcome mo-4-1: Explain the SI combustion process, analyze engine knock including mitigation strategies, and evaluate advanced SI combustion strategies Module outcome mo-4-2: Explain the four phases of diesel combustion, analyze fuel spray behavior, and evaluate the NOx-PM trade-off Module outcome mo-4-3: Compare thermodynamic cycles, analyze Atkinson/Miller cycle principles, and evaluate advanced combustion modes

modules.title: Emissions - The Constraint That Defines Modern Engine Design
modules.note: Emission formation, after-treatment systems, regulations, and diagnostics Module outcome mo-5-1: Explain the formation mechanisms for NOx, CO, HC, and PM, and evaluate the NOx-PM trade-off to propose reduction strategies Module outcome mo-5-2: Explain Three-Way Catalyst operation, design integrated diesel after-treatment systems, and evaluate SCR systems Module outcome mo-5-3: Compare global emission regulations, explain OBD-II architecture, and diagnose emission system faults using diagnostic data

modules.title: Advanced Technologies & Future Directions
topics: Thermal Management, Friction Reduction & System Integration
modules.note: Alternate fuels, energy transition, thermal management, and efficiency optimization Module outcome mo-6-1: Evaluate properties and combustion characteristics of alternate fuels, assess engine modifications, and analyze IC engines in future mobility Module outcome mo-6-2: Analyze heat transfer mechanisms, evaluate friction reduction strategies, assess waste heat recovery, and integrate efficiency technologies

objectives.text: Analyze engine architecture, performance parameters, and calibration strategies to optimize torque, power, thermal efficiency, and fuel consumption for both SI and CI engines in real-world applications
Design and evaluate air intake, fuel injection, and charge motion systems to maximize volumetric efficiency, mixture quality, and combustion performance while meeting power and emissions targets
Analyze combustion processes in SI and CI engines, diagnose combustion-related issues using thermodynamic principles and diagnostic data, and apply advanced combustion strategies
Evaluate emission formation mechanisms and design integrated emission control strategies combining in-cylinder measures and after-treatment systems to achieve regulatory compliance
Assess the technical and economic feasibility of advanced engine technologies, alternate fuels, efficiency improvements, and hybrid powertrains for future mobility and industrial applications

Analyze Atkinson/Miller cycle principles and evaluate their implementation using variable valve timing
Evaluate advanced combustion modes (HCCI, RCCI, PCCI) including their benefits and challenges
Assess variable compression ratio technology and its potential for efficiency and performance optimization
Explain the formation mechanisms for NOx (thermal Zeldovich), CO (incomplete oxidation), HC (crevices, quench), and PM (soot formation/oxidation)
Analyze the factors affecting each pollutant (temperature, mixture ratio, mixing, oxygen availability)
Evaluate the NOx-PM trade-off in diesel engines and explain why in-cylinder optimization alone is insufficient
Identify emission sources for different engine operating conditions and propose in-cylinder reduction strategies
Explain the operation of Three-Way Catalysts (TWC) and the importance of stoichiometric operation
Design integrated after-treatment systems for diesel engines (DOC, DPF, SCR)

Analyze the role of IC engines in future mobility scenarios including hybridization and synthetic fuels

sessions.title: Build Your Engine - Architecture, Power, Thermodynamics

blocks.title: Hook
blocks.activity: *Gamification intro:* "You're an engine designer. Here's the spec: Design an engine for [delivery truck / sports car / generator]. What choices will you make?" Show 3 contrasting engine images: Formula 1 V6 turbo, heavy-duty diesel truck, industrial generator Ask: "What makes these engines different? By end of session, you'll know how to design for each application."

blocks.title: Objectives & Recall
blocks.activity: State 4 session outcomes clearly Activate prior knowledge: "What do you already know about engines from undergrad or work?" Session roadmap: Architecture → Performance metrics → Thermodynamics → Components → Design exercise

Bore & stroke (7 min): Define oversquare, square, undersquare with diagrams Effect on piston speed, breathing, torque character Show diesel (undersquare) vs F1 (oversquare) comparison Calculation demo: Displacemen

BMEP (8 min): Best metric for comparison (displacement-independent) Formula: BMEP = (Brake power × 1

sessions.title: Build Your Engine - Breathing & Control Systems

blocks.title: Hook
blocks.activity: "Your engine from Session 1 needs to breathe and control itself. How do we optimize the 4-stroke cycle?" Show video: High-speed intake valve motion (30 sec) - "Air flow is pulsating, not steady!"

blocks.title: Objectives & Recall
blocks.activity: Recall Session 1: We designed engine architecture. Now: How does it actually run? Today: 4-stroke cycle → VE → VVT → Control systems

blocks.title: Part 1: 4-Stroke Cycle Deep Dive
blocks.activity: Each stroke (5 min each): Intake, compression, power, exhaust Describe what's happening Valve position, pressure in cylinder Energy flow (negative work on compression, positive on power) Valve overlap (5 min): Both valves open near TDC - why? Benefits: Scavenging, reduced pumping Drawbacks: Low-speed torque loss, HC emissions VVT optimizes across RPM range

blocks.title: MCQ #1
blocks.activity: Valve overlap effects (Q1-2-3)

blocks.title: Part 2: Volumetric Efficiency
blocks.activity: Definition (5 min): VE = Actual air mass / Theoretical air mass Typical: 75-95% NA, >100% with boost/tuning Calculation demo Factors affecting VE (15 min): Valve flow: Size, lift, duration, # of valves Port design: Smooth flow vs charge motion trade-off Manifold: Runner length/diameter tuning Temperature: Cooler = denser Speed: VE vs RPM curve (peaks then drops) Improving VE (5 min): Larger valves

blocks.title: MCQ #2
blocks.activity: VE calculation (Q1-2-1)

blocks.title: Part 3: Variable Valve Timing
blocks.activity: Why VVT (3 min): Optimize valve timing across RPM/load Technologies (7 min): Cam phasing (most common) Dual VVT, profile switching (VTEC), variable lift Benefits at each condition: Low RPM (reduce overlap), high RPM (increase overlap), part load (late closing for Atkinson effect) Cylinder deactivation (5 min): Shut off cylinders at light load → improve BSFC

blocks.title: Part 3: Variable Valve Timing
blocks.activity: Why VVT (3 min): Optimize valve timing across RPM/load Technologies (7 min): Cam phasing (most common) Dual VVT, profile switching (VTEC), variable lift Benefits at each condition: Low RPM (reduce overlap), high RPM (increase overlap), part load (late closing for Atkinson effect) Cylinder deactivation (5 min): Shut off cylinders at light load → improve BSFC

blocks.title: Part 4: Engine Control Systems
blocks.activity: ECU architecture (5 min): Inputs (sensors) → Processing (maps, calculations) → Outputs (actuators) Key sensors (4 min): MAF, MAP, TPS, O2, knock, temp, crank/cam position Show physical sensors if available Key actuators (3 min): Injectors, ignition coils, VVT solenoids, throttle Control loops (3 min): Open loop vs closed loop Example: AFR control using O2 sensor feedback

blocks.title: MCQ #3
blocks.activity: O2 sensor for closed-loop control (Q1-2-2)

blocks.title: Interactive Diagnostic Exercise
blocks.activity: Scenario: Engine runs rough, poor fuel economy, black smoke. MAF reading high, O2 sensor shows rich. Question: What failed? Answer: MAF over-reading → ECU adds too much fuel Brief discussion

blocks.title: Wrap-up
blocks.activity: Breathing + control = performance Module 1 complete: You can now design an engine (architecture + breathing + control) Reminder: SLP due before Session 3 - peer presentations will happen

blocks.title: Part 3: Operating Parameters
blocks.activity: Spark timing - SI (12 min): MBT timing, knock-limited timing Advancing vs retarding - effects Spark map: RPM × load → timing Factors: Load, RPM, temperature, octane, EGR Injection timing - CI (10 min): Advancing → efficiency, NOx; Retarding → lower NOx, PM Injection pressure effects Multi-pulse injection Compression ratio (4 min): Higher CR → higher efficiency Limits: Knock (SI), mechanical (CI) M

Fuel, timing, VVT, boost, EGR, lambda, transients, diagnostics Challenge (5 min): Cannot optimize all simultaneously - trade-offs Triangle of doom: Power, emissions, fuel economy Must prioritize

sessions.title: Thermal Management, Friction Reduction & System Integration

blocks.title: Hook
blocks.activity: "We've covered engine fundamentals, performance, air/fuel, combustion, emissions, future fuels. Now: How do we squeeze out every last percent of efficiency?" Show efficiency breakdown pie chart: 40% useful work, 30% coolant, 30% exhaust - "Can we recover the 60% waste?"

blocks.title: Part 1: Heat Transfer & Thermal Management
blocks.activity: Heat transfer mechanisms: Conduction, convection, radiation Where heat is lost: Coolant, exhaust, oil, radiation Strategies to reduce heat loss: Insulated combustion chamber, thermal barrier coatings

blocks.title: MCQ #1
blocks.activity: Waste heat recovery (Q6-15-1)

blocks.title: Part 2: Friction Reduction
blocks.activity: Friction sources: Piston/rings, bearings, valvetrain, accessories Friction increases with speed² Reduction strategies: Low-viscosity oils, coatings, roller followers, reduced tension rings Trade-offs: Adequate lubrication vs friction

blocks.title: MCQ #2
blocks.activity: Low-viscosity oil trade-off (Q6-15-2)

blocks.title: Part 3: Waste Heat Recovery Technologies
blocks.activity: Turbocompound: Extract work from exhaust after turbo ORC (Organic Rankine Cycle): Use exhaust heat to drive secondary power cycle TEG (Thermoelectric Generator): Convert heat to electricity Efficiency gains: 3-5% for turbocompound, 2-4% for ORC Cost-benefit: Best for steady-state, high-utilization applications (long-haul trucks)

blocks.title: Part 4: System Integration & Downsizing
blocks.activity: Engine downsizing: Smaller displacement + turbo = better part-load efficiency Hybridization: IC engine operates at optimal efficiency, electric fills gaps Cylinder deactivation, start-stop, sailing Multiple technologies combined: Downsizing + direct injection + VVT + turbo + mild hybrid
